title: Polish B1 Exam: Citizenship Rules, Modules and Prep Plan
excerpt: The Polish B1 exam for citizenship explained: who needs it, the four written modules, the 50% pass rule, registration and a realistic study plan.
metaDescription: The Polish B1 exam for citizenship explained: who needs it, the four written modules, the 50% pass rule, registration and a realistic study plan.
summary: To be recognised as a Polish citizen by the voivode, adults must prove Polish at B1 or higher with a state certificate or a Polish-language school certificate.
The adult Polish B1 exam has four written modules (listening, reading, grammar, writing) lasting up to 190 minutes in total, plus an oral part of up to 15 minutes.
You must score at least 50% in every written module and in the oral part; the scores are not averaged.
You register with an authorised exam centre, not the State Commission, and fees and procedures change under a law amendment from 1 January 2027.

factNotes: certyfikatpolski.pl sits behind a Cloudflare JS challenge and the Wayback Machine rate-limited me, so I could open only the homepage and fees page snapshots directly. All structural rules (modules, 190/15 min limits, 50%-per-module pass rule, registration ≥1 month before, results, devices) are taken from the 2025 regulation text itself. Session months (2026: Feb, Apr, Jun, Oct, Dec for adult B1; 2027 published July 2026), 'centre lists published ~2 months ahead', equal points per written module and the Feb 2026 foreign centres (Germany, USA) come from search-engine snippets of official certyfikatpolski.pl pages, so I gave months only (no exact days) and told readers to check. Left out: per-module minutes (official table and sample papers disagree: 25 vs 30/40 min for listening) and exact point totals (30/30/30/30 + 40 oral per the snippet). The pending 2025-2026 citizenship bills are mentioned only as 'debated'; their status is unclear (one source says rejected) and the consolidated Act still requires B1. '18 months to 2 years from zero' is framed as our own planning estimate, anchored only by the FSI figure (which targets a higher level). Certificate expiry: neither act sets one; hedged with 'ask your voivodeship office'. Post-2027 regulation details (modules, pass marks) will be set by a new regulation not yet published; flagged in the top note.
